vocabulary._description: The grammar pin gate (script/m14/verify-grammar-pins.ts) reports three counts for this lane -- ids=301 namedUnique=36 anonUnique=104 fields=2 -- and this file uses the same three so the two documents can be compared directly. `ids` is tree-sitter's whole symbol space and mixes three vocabularies; `namedUnique`/`anonUnique` are its two halves by tree-sitter's OWN nodeTypeIsNamed flag, not by a pattern on the name. This spec buckets by ANALYZER REACHABILITY, a different axis and deliberately not the same partition: `internal_silent` holds anonymous tokens (punctuation, the `---`/`...` document markers) and the two grammar-internal wrappers. The two axes are reconciled in `internal_silent.named_vs_anonymous`.
vocabulary.fieldsNote: fieldCount=2 is the entire field surface of this grammar, and the analyzer reads BOTH through childForFieldName (real-yaml-analyzer.ts:204 `childForFieldName("value")`, :506 `childForFieldName("key")`). This is the one structural property that makes the lane pure-AST by construction: the mapping-pair key and value are addressable by field, so no part of the extraction needs to look at a delimiter or at character offsets in the source.
vocabulary.anonymousTypesNote: 102 anonymous / hidden token types the wired 0.7.1 wasm produces, listed as data rather than as classification rows. None can be a symbol: an anonymous node is a token the grammar never names, and the analyzer reads tokens through their parent's fields (`key`/`value` — the grammar's entire field surface, 2 fields) rather than by visiting tokens directly.

measured._description: Every count here was produced by script/m14/tmp/yaml-f8-census.ts over 1,274 files drawn from EIGHT pinned repositories, walking every named AND anonymous child. The probe is committed so the next reader re-runs it and gets these numbers; nothing in this section is carried over from a previous wave.

handled_verified._description: Analyzer-referenced node types, each with the count that proves it was reached in real code rather than recognised by name. A type counts as HANDLED when the analyzer names it in a node-type position AND it was observed in the eight-repo corpus. Handled does NOT mean "emits a symbol": the analyzer can handle a construct by consciously emitting nothing for it, and `flow_node` and `block_node` do exactly that (they are grammar wrappers whose only role is to carry an anchor, a tag, or the real value, and the analyzer reads through them). The distinction that matters is handled vs unexamined: nothing in this list is merely unaccounted for. The 8 DIRECTIVE types join the list as of 2026-09-27 (`yaml_version`, `tag_handle`, `tag_prefix`, `directive_name`, `directive_parameter`, `yaml_directive`, `tag_directive`, `reserved_directive`): the analyzer reads %YAML and %TAG directives into `metadata.yamlVersion` / `metadata.reservedDirectives`, resolves a `!handle!name` tag through the %TAG prefix it declares, and reports a reserved directive it does not implement rather than ignoring it. `comment` and `tag` also move here from the gap table, which is kept below as the record of what was open and when it closed. ERROR and MISSING are classified here deliberately: the completeness gate force-appends both to the wasm's named-type list so that a lane cannot leave them unclassified, and the lane DOES handle them — a grammar-error subtree is re-rooted under a `#damaged@<line>` scope with stable per-child identity, pinned by fixture `error-recovery-identity` and mutant `yaml/recovery-scope-renamed`. An ERROR is the grammar reporting that it could not lex; publishing it as a scope is how a configuration language stays navigable when a file is wrong.

resolved_via_parent.alias: alias -> alias_name (the anchor reference; resolved to the anchor's identity, emitted as uses/extends)
resolved_via_parent.alias_name: alias_name is the child of alias and carries the referenced anchor's name
resolved_via_parent.anchor: anchor -> anchor_name (the anchor definition; emitted as a constant under the value it names)
resolved_via_parent.anchor_name: anchor_name is the child of anchor and carries the anchor's name
resolved_via_parent.block_node: block_node -> block_mapping | block_sequence | anchor | tag (a pure wrapper; the analyzer reads through it via valueType)
resolved_via_parent.flow_node: flow_node -> plain_scalar | flow_mapping | flow_sequence | alias | anchor | tag (a pure wrapper; same)
resolved_via_parent.plain_scalar: plain_scalar -> boolean_scalar | integer_scalar | float_scalar | null_scalar | string_scalar (the core schema's dispatch target: which child it holds IS the resolved type)
resolved_via_parent.stream: stream -> document | comment (the file-level container; drives documentCount and comment attribution)

wrapper_handling._description: `block_node` and `flow_node` are the two nodes that make a value addressable without a field, and they are the reason the analyzer can stay field-driven. Neither emits a symbol; both are read through by `valueType` and by `scalarText`.

handled_verified.core_schema_note: `plain_scalar` is a DISPATCH node, not a type. Under the wired build (see design_decision YAML-D6) a plain scalar's resolved type is decided by which of boolean_scalar/integer_scalar/float_scalar/null_scalar/string_scalar the grammar attached. Every one of those five is listed above and every one is observed in the corpus, so the dispatch is evidenced at both ends rather than assumed.

internal_silent._description: Named grammar types the analyzer deliberately does NOT turn into a declaration, each with a reason. This list is NAMED TYPES ONLY, and that is a contract with the completeness inventory rather than a style choice: the gate enumerates the wasm's NAMED node types and reports any row here that the wasm does not produce as GRAMMAR DRIFT. The first draft of this spec also listed 104 anonymous and `_`-prefixed token types here, and the gate correctly reported all 104 as rows the grammar no longer produces — an anonymous token can never appear in a named-type enumeration, so the finding was about the spec's shape, not the grammar. They are recorded as vocabulary in `vocabulary.anonymousTypes` where a count belongs, and no anonymous type is ever a declaration candidate in any case. `escape_sequence` and `timestamp_scalar` live here rather than only in the gap table because the gate classifies a gap row through its `node_type` field and these are defect-style records that carry none — so leaving the types out of every bucket would have reported 11 real node types as unclassified.

named_vs_anonymous._note: All 15 observed anonymous types are structural punctuation: " : - ? [ ] { } , & * ' | > and the --- / ... document markers. The remaining 89 anonymous types are hidden `_rules`, `_repeatN` and `_tokenN` wrappers that never appear as nodes in a concrete tree. Punctuation emits nothing because it IS nothing: in a data language a `:` does not declare a symbol, the pair around it does.

never_observed_named._description: Nine NAMED types the grammar declares that occur ZERO times in 1,274 files across eight independent repositories. Each carries the mechanism that explains it. These are the rows the blind-spot detector exists for: without them they would read as unmeasured holes, and the honest answer for each is different.
never_observed_named.directive_name: 0 occurrences. A child of reserved_directive (`%FOO bar baz`). Reserved directives are removed from the YAML 1.2 spec, so real-world usage is near-zero by design. Mechanism: the construct is deprecated upstream, not unreachable in this build.
never_observed_named.directive_parameter: 0 occurrences. The parameters of a reserved_directive. Same mechanism as directive_name.
never_observed_named.reserved_directive: 0 occurrences. `%FOO bar baz` -- removed from YAML 1.2. Ruled internal_silent with the reason 'deprecated by the specification', not 'unreachable'.
never_observed_named.tag_directive: 0 occurrences across all eight corpora, but REACHABLE and measured: `%TAG !e! tag:example.com,2000:` parses as (document (tag_directive (tag_handle) (tag_prefix)) ...) with tag_handle.text=\"!e!\" and tag_prefix.text=\"tag:example.com,2000:\" (script/m14/tmp/yaml-tag-visibility.ts). Absent from these corpora because %TAG is a schema-authoring tool and none of the eight repos ships YAML schemas. The analyzer handles it (see gap YAML-G3, closed by the directive work).
never_observed_named.tag_handle: 0 occurrences. Child of tag_directive. Reachable, measured, handled -- see tag_directive.
never_observed_named.tag_prefix: 0 occurrences. Child of tag_directive. Reachable, measured, handled -- see tag_directive.
never_observed_named.yaml_directive: 0 occurrences across all eight corpora, but REACHABLE and measured: `%YAML 1.1` parses as (document (yaml_directive (yaml_version)) ...) with yaml_version.text=\"1.1\" (same probe). Absent from these corpora because %YAML is implicit in all of them -- every one is YAML 1.2, which is the default, so nobody writes the directive. Handled (see gap YAML-G3).
never_observed_named.yaml_version: 0 occurrences. Child of yaml_directive. Reachable, measured, handled -- see yaml_directive.
never_observed_named.timestamp_scalar: 0 occurrences, and this one has a NAMED MECHANISM rather than a corpus explanation. The grammar's external scanner selects between three alternative scalar-resolution backends at build time (grammars/tree-sitter-yaml/src/scanner.c:7-11: `#ifndef YAML_SCHEMA` / `#define YAML_SCHEMA core` / `#include _file(YAML_SCHEMA)`), and the wired wasm is the `core` build. src/schema.core.c sets `HAS_TIMESTAMP 0`; src/schema.legacy.c sets `HAS_TIMESTAMP 1` and is the only backend that adds an `RS_TIMESTAMP` resolution result. Measured consequence under the wired build: BOTH `at: 2001-12-14` and `at: 2001-12-14t21:59:43.10-05:00` parse as (flow_node (plain_scalar (string_scalar))) -- not timestamp_scalar. So the type is declared in node-types.json AND present in the wired wasm's 36 named types, and the wired build's scanner never produces it. Ruled internal_silent with the mechanism recorded, and NOT a fixture: writing a fixture for a node this build cannot emit is the provenance theatre #288 was called out for. See design_decision YAML-D6 for the limitation this creates.

gap._description: Every named grammar type is accounted for in exactly one of three places: handled_verified (emitted and measured), internal_silent (deliberately not a declaration, with the reason), or a gap row here. A type that is none of the three is a blind spot. As of 2026-09-27 the two gaps this spec opened are CLOSED (YAML-G1 comments, YAML-G3 tags) and the two that remain are RULED internal_silent with a mechanism (YAML-G2 escape_sequence, YAML-G4 timestamp_scalar), so the open-gap count is 0 — which is a statement about the four rows in this file, not a claim that the lane is complete.

gaps.why: The analyzer has no comment handling of any kind. A comment is a stream-level sibling of document, carries its own text including the leading '#', and is the documentation surface of a configuration language -- yet 7,938 real comments across all eight corpora produce no docstring, no metadata and no symbol. Matrix 1b lists docstrings as a required payload and the store binds symbol.docstring.
gaps.ruling: CLOSED 2026-09-27 by the analyzer work this gap was opened for, and the spec is updated rather than left claiming an open hole. Comments are now read as document-level stream siblings and attributed POSITIONALLY, not textually: a comment immediately preceding a key at the same or shallower column documents that key, anything else is file-level. Pinned by fixtures `comment-attribution` and `comment-attribution-negative` (the negative twin exists because attribution that fires on every comment is the failure mode, not a fix) and by mutant `yaml/comment-banner-stolen`, which reverts the attribution and is caught. The 'no comment handling of any kind' statement above is the PRE-work census and is kept as the record of what was measured, not as a current claim.

gaps.why: The most frequent unnamed type in the entire lane. An escape_sequence is a token INSIDE a quoted scalar (\\n, \\", \\u00e9), not a construct that declares anything. The analyzer's scalarText reads the parent scalar's text whole, so the escapes are already carried in the emitted value; what is missing is that the analyzer cannot say WHICH escapes a value contains.
gaps.ruling: RULED internal_silent, with the reason stated: an escape is part of its scalar's spelling, and YAML has no declaration attached to one. The alternative -- emitting a symbol per escape -- would be 11,923 phantom declarations in the corpus, which is the fabrication the M14 contract exists to prevent. Recorded as a decision rather than left silent.

gaps.why: The corpus understates this badly and the spec has to say so. 7 occurrences in 1,274 files, and a tag census across all eight repos shows every one of them is a cipher marker (!vault, !unsafe) or a JMESPath fragment, never a type annotation. The construct is far more load-bearing than its corpus count suggests: a YAML tag IS the language's only type annotation, and `!!str 7` is currently classified valueType=integer because the analyzer reads straight through the tag to the scalar underneath. Separately, `!include other.yml` produces zero symbols and zero relationships, which makes a real cross-file import invisible.
gaps.ruling: CLOSED 2026-09-27, and M60 R9 (the declared-type reference graph) now MEASURES the closure rather than merely permitting it. A YAML tag is the language's only declared-type position: the capability was absent until this round — `tag` was in no handled set, so `!!str 7` reported valueType=integer and the tag was read straight through. Four forms are emitted as a closed `declared_type` edge: `!!local`, `!custom`, `!<verbatim>`, and `!handle!name` resolved through a %TAG directive. Pinned by fixtures `tag-declared-type` and `tag-declared-type-negative`, plus `directive-tag-handle` for the directive form. The capability row is measured by script/m60/declared-type-refs-census.ts, which reads `present-declared_type` for yaml (declared=2 typeRefs=2 control=y) after a yaml snippet was added to its table; the lane's reading is recorded in validation/m60/declared-type-register.json. The 7 corpus occurrences still badly understate the construct, as recorded above — that part of the finding was true and remains true.

gaps.why: See internal_silent.never_observed_named.timestamp_scalar -- the wired build is the core schema and never produces this node.
gaps.ruling: RULED internal_silent, mechanism recorded. Carried in design_decision YAML-D6 as a declared limitation because the same mechanism has a user-visible consequence.

design_decision.description: Constructs YAML has no grammar node for, or has no axis for at all. Each is RULED with its reason rather than left as an absence, because 'the language cannot express it' and 'the analyzer forgot it' look identical in an output diff and are not the same finding.

decisions.decision: No `calls` relationship. YAML has no call expression: there is no way to write one in the grammar, so the analyzer has nothing to read.
decisions.why: Claiming `calls` for a language with no call expression would be coverage theatre. The M14 spec is explicit that `requiredKinds` must be the kinds a language ACTUALLY emits, not the schema's full list.

decisions.decision: No `implements`, no `overrides`, no `instantiates`. YAML has no object-orientation axis: no class declaration, no method, no member lookup that resolves to a declaration site.
decisions.why: Same reasoning as YAML-D1. Merge keys (`<<: *anchor`) are the one genuine inheritance construct YAML has, and they are emitted as `extends` with the anchor as the target -- which is the closest honest mapping, not a stand-in for a missing feature.

decisions.decision: No `visibility` payload. YAML has no access-level axis: there is no private/package/public in the language, and every key is equally addressable.
decisions.why: An element of configuration is not an access level. Emitting `visibility: public` for every symbol would fill a Matrix 1b cell with a constant that carries no information.

decisions.decision: No `typeParameters`/`genericParameters` payload. YAML has no parameterised types.
decisions.why: The construct a tag fills -- naming a type -- is carried instead by the declared-type reference graph (M60 R9): a `references` edge from the declaration that writes the tag to the type the tag names, marked metadata.relationshipType === "declared_type". That is the honest home for YAML's type information, and it is a graph edge rather than a symbol field because a YAML tag names a type used AT a position, it does not parameterise a declaration.

decisions.decision: `imports`/`exports` are emitted from tag and key SHAPES, not from a grammar construct. YAML has no import keyword.
decisions.why: The constructs that genuinely import another file are `!include`/`!import` tags (Ansible) and a CI step's `uses:` key (GitHub Actions). Both are addressable purely from node type and position -- a tag whose text names a tag-handle plus a path-like scalar, and a mapping pair whose key node's text is `uses`. Measured corpus support is uneven and declared as such: 237 `uses:` sites across gh-cli's 25 files, and ZERO `!include` in any of the eight corpora, so the tag half rests on fixtures.

decisions.decision: The wired grammar is the `core` (YAML 1.2) schema build, and a file that opens `%YAML 1.1` is still resolved with 1.2 scalar rules. Declared as a limitation rather than worked around.
decisions.why: grammars/tree-sitter-yaml/src/scanner.c:7-11 selects the backend at compile time and the published wasm is the `core` one. YAML 1.1 and 1.2 genuinely disagree (`yes`/`no`/`on`/`off` as booleans, octal 0777, sexagesimal 1:30), and no build of this grammar resolves a 1.1 file with 1.1 rules while also being the published artifact. Switching to the `legacy` backend would mean replacing the newest published bytes with a local build whose entire gain is one scalar type, and would make this lane's typing disagree with every YAML 1.2 consumer reading the same file. The decision is therefore to PIN the core build and DECLARE the limitation, and to record the declined alternative with its measurement in the grammar pin's `alternatives` (script/m14/verify-grammar-pins.ts, lane yaml). Changing what is shipped is a separate act with its own A/B under script/m14/verify-grammar-leaves.ts.

decisions.decision: An anonymous scalar sequence item is a VALUE, not a declaration, and does not become a symbol. An object- or array-valued sequence item DOES, as `item_<index>` under the parent path plus `[index]`.
decisions.why: src/ast/parallel-indexer.ts:2390-2394 names YAML merge keys as a legitimate symbol contract that must survive the name filter, and the parallel-indexer comment records that the narrow filter is applied to verified analyzer output precisely for contracts like this. A list of strings is data; a list of objects is a set of records, and the records are what a reader navigates to.

decisions.decision: Duplicate mapping keys in one mapping get disambiguated identities rather than one shared identity.
decisions.why: Duplicate keys are invalid YAML, so this is not a shape to model -- it is a shape to survive. Two symbols sharing one id and one qualifiedName makes every relationship endpoint addressed to that key ambiguous, because the graph resolves relationships by qualified name while the store's own primary key is `${fileId}:${name}:${startLine}` (src/ast/parallel-indexer.ts:2259). The analyzer must therefore keep its identities at least as specific as the store's, or it silently loses an edge.
